title: Lists: Keeping Many Values in Order
concepts: building a list in a loop

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Asked for the three biggest sales, the AI sorted the list with sort() and took sales[:3], and said it would print [21.0, 15.75, 12.5]. sort() puts the smallest first, so the code printed the three smallest sales, [6.5, 8.0, 9.25]. Checking the first item against max(sales) catches it; sort(reverse=True) fixes it.

changes: Nested lists, comprehensions, extend(), index(), count(), del and enumerate() are left out to keep one new idea per step; comprehensions follow in Chapter 14.
The in operator is taught here for lists; it had not been used in earlier chapters.
The AI section adds verified files for each stage: a worked slice example, a test of three lists, the sort() None error and a suggestion that changes the order of the output.
outstanding_issues: The tracebacks show the short file name; on a learner's computer the full path appears instead.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
